label: Blue Note
rationale: Identified by Scott Yanow in his AllMusic 'Hard Bop' essay as one of 17 Essential Hard Bop Recordings; 4.5 stars from both AllMusic and the Penguin Guide. Recorded March 26, 1961 with the same rhythm section as Soul Station (Kelly/Chambers/Jones) plus Grant Green, it is the companion peak to a Mobley run already anchored in the canon by Soul Station and Roll Call. Session gravity is exceptional: five musicians each already load-bearing in the network.

personnel_record.notes: Single session, March 26, 1961 (Wikipedia S1; AllMusic S2 confirms date and Van Gelder Studios NJ). Released March 1962 as BST 84080. Engineer not named in sources; Rudy Van Gelder assigned per the Van Gelder-inference rule (Blue Note, 1961, Van Gelder Studio confirmed) — engineer field is inf even though epistemic_production reflects producer/studio obs. AllMusic (S2) tags styles Hard Bop / Guitar Jazz / Saxophone Jazz and dates release 1961 (recording date); Wikipedia gives March 1962 release. Track 6 is a CD bonus track; a second alternate take of 'Three Coins in the Fountain' appears only on the 2014 SHM-CD and is excluded. Yanow 'Hard Bop' essay citation via Wikipedia reference [4]. Per-track personnel not itemized in sources; full quintet assumed on all tracks, track_assignments_complete=false.

ballot.case_for: Workout is an exceptionally lucid, durable hard-bop statement: Mobley's relaxed melodic logic, Grant Green's guitar, and the Wynton Kelly–Paul Chambers–Philly Joe Jones rhythm section create a deeply swinging, immediately accessible Blue Note quintet sound. The dossier identifies Scott Yanow's placement of the album among 17 Essential Hard Bop Recordings and reports 4.5-star assessments from both AllMusic and the Penguin Guide, giving it meaningful cross-publication critical support. Its personnel also make it a major network session, joining the late Miles Davis rhythm-section engine to Mobley and Green at defining moments in their Blue Note work.
ballot.case_against: Its claim is stronger as a superb consolidation than as a decisive historical turning point: Soul Station is the more singular Mobley defining statement, while Workout largely extends a closely related early-1960s hard-bop language and personnel world. The consensus evidence is favorable but not extensively triangulated in the dossier: Yanow is one critic's essential list, while the Penguin rating is asserted without a supplied source, and the substantive documentation relies chiefly on Wikipedia and AllMusic. Track-level personnel are assumed rather than independently documented, so the research file is less robust than the musical reputation warrants.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes that John treat Workout as a strong consensus-core addition to the hard-bop canon, while preserving Soul Station as Mobley's more indispensable single defining record.
